newsitem.title: USA: Reebok CEO says Olympics boosted sales.
newsitem.headline: Reebok CEO says Olympics boosted sales.

text.p: Reebok International Ltd Chairman and Chief Executive Officer Paul Fireman said on Thursday the Atlanta Olympics provided a boost in sales for the sneaker and apparel maker.
After the Olympics, the Stoughton, Mass.-based firm experienced "a boost in our sales in apparel, particularly overseas in European and Asian markets," he told a news conference.
Reebok outfitted a number of Eureopean and Asian teams, and each country's team was spotlighted on local television, he said.
Fireman declined to give specific numbers for post-Olympics sales.
He said he was pleased with the results of a self-tender offer made over the summer that garnered 17 million shares.
He also said he was pleased by the actions of bond rating agencies that "kept us at investment grade."
"That was good," he said. "It saved us a lot of money."
He declined to discuss third quarter results but said, "We have a task ahead of us to make the company stronger and to bring it back to healthier market share."

Fireman's news conference followed a meeting with the Executive Forum of the Greater Boston Chamber of Commerce, where he announced that he had invited Phil Knight, chairman and CEO of Nike Inc, to join him in developing an independent monitoring system that would guard against abusive working conditions in footwear industry factories worldwide.
